summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Dihybrid Cross (RRYY × rryy) yields F1 RrYy (Round Yellow). F2 generation produces 4 phenotypic classes in 9:3:3:1 ratio and 9 distinct genotypic classes (1:2:1:2:4:2:1:2:1). Test cross determines unknown dominant genotype by crossing with homozygous recessive parent (Monohybrid test cross: 1:1; Dihybrid test cross: 1:1:1:1).

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 2.1 Dihybrid Cross Mechanics

$$\text{Dihybrid Cross: } RRYY \text{ (Round Yellow)} \times rryy \text{ (Wrinkled Green)} \longrightarrow F_1: RrYy \text{ (Round Yellow)}$$

$$F_2 \text{ Phenotypic Ratio} = \mathbf{9:3:3:1}$$

$$\text{(9 Round Yellow : 3 Round Green : 3 Wrinkled Yellow : 1 Wrinkled Green)}$$

$$F_2 \text{ Genotypic Ratio} = \mathbf{1:2:1:2:4:2:1:2:1} \quad (9\text{ distinct genotypes})$$

### 2.2 Test Cross Mechanics
- **Definition**: Crossing an individual exhibiting a dominant phenotype ($T\_$) with a homozygous recessive parent ($tt$) to determine whether the dominant individual is homozygous ($TT$) or heterozygous ($Tt$).
  - If $TT \times tt \longrightarrow 100\%$ Tall (Homozygous Dominant).
  - If $Tt \times tt \longrightarrow \mathbf{1:1}$ ratio ($50\%$ Tall : $50\%$ Dwarf) (Heterozygous).
- **Dihybrid Test Cross**: $RrYy \times rryy \longrightarrow \mathbf{1:1:1:1}$ ($25\%$ Round Yellow : $25\%$ Round Green : $25\%$ Wrinkled Yellow : $25\%$ Wrinkled Green).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Back Cross vs Test Cross
conceptBreakdown.title: Back Cross vs Test Cross
conceptBreakdown.content: Every test cross is a back cross (crossing F1 with any parent), but not every back cross is a test cross (which specifically requires the homozygous recessive parent).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Forked-Line Probability Method
conceptBreakdown.title: Forked-Line Probability Method
conceptBreakdown.content: Multi-locus phenotypic ratios can be computed as the product of independent monohybrid ratios: $(3:1) \times (3:1) = 9:3:3:1$ for dihybrids; $(3:1)^3 = 27:9:9:9:3:3:3:1$ for trihybrids.
